messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up: I've been prototyping an ingress "split-and-stitch" flow to keep alerts fast while keeping full-fidelity traces for billing/analytics. Want feedback on failure modes before I write the RFC.

Priya: nice. what does "stitch" look like? a join keyed by trace id later?

Alex: plan: at ingress we emit two records: a light envelope (fast-path) and a full envelope (backfill-path). We include a small, stable stitch_token when available (from SDKs). If stitch_token missing, backfill-path will produce a reattach message that references the fast-path event id.

Ben: reattach message sounds right, but watch ordering. If reattach arrives after TTL for fast-path, alerts might miss the billing update.

Nina: agree. propose timelines: fast-path TTL >= alert SLO window + grace. e.g., if alerts check 5m windows, keep fast-path 15m before compacting.

Priya: compacting policy is important. Also how do we avoid duplicates when stitch_token is present both in SDK and produced by enrichers? Need dedupe id or canonicalizer.

Alex: good point. I'll add canonicalization rules: prefer SDK-provided stitch_token, else use generated hash(trace_id, tenant). Dedupe sets on aggregator side use (tenant, stitch_token) as primary key.

Ben: infra note: shard keys for both paths must align to avoid cross-partition joins. If backfill-topic gets a different hash we get cross-shard joins with higher latency.

Nina: maybe use a unified partition key: tenant_id||shard_hint. That keeps both records colocated.

Alex: agreed. Another piece: reconciliation job that scans backfill-topic for events that didn't attach and emits "reattach-candidate" to a hotpath topic for the billing service to consume and update attribution. This job needs idempotency and at-least-once semantics.

Priya: how will billing UI surface retro-attributed changes? We should mark rows as "initial" vs "reconciled" and show reconciliation timestamp. Customers hate surprise charges.

Ben: SLA for reconciliation? We can't leave gaps longer than a billing window (24h) otherwise invoice mismatches. Suggest default maximum reconciliation latency of 6h, configurable per tenant.

Nina: also think about cost: scanning backfill-topic for missed joins could be expensive. Instead, emit counters at ingress when stitch_token absent, and run targeted reattach for those IDs only.

Alex: yep, counters + a compacted index of missing_ids per tenant reduces work. Implementation sketch:

```
ingress:
  emit_fast: true
  emit_backfill: true
  stitch_policy: prefer_sdk|generate
  partition_key: tenant_id|trace_hash
backfill:
  topic: telemetry.backfill.v1
  retention_days: 90
reconcile:
  max_latency_hours: 6
  scan_strategy: targeted  # options: full-scan|targeted
```

Priya: one more: metric and span correlation. If we split, we must ensure trace->metric links (for trace-backed alerts) remain intact. That means linking by trace_id in both envelopes.

Ben: and logs too. The log router must copy trace_id into log envelopes or we lose cross-signal joins.

Nina: failure modes to call out in RFC: missing stitch_token rollout, cross-shard reattach, stale fast-paths, dedupe false-positives, and reconciliation lag. We should include mitigations for each.

Alex: thanks. I'll draft RFC with diagrams and cost projections. Plan to run a 2-week canary on non-prod tenants with stitch_token generation enabled server-side to measure reattach traffic.

ingest-bot: NOTE: prototype branch created refs/heads/ingress-split-stitch-proto (CI queued). :rocket:

Priya: +1 to canary. Ben/Nina want to own the reconciliation runner and partitioning tests?

Ben: I'll own runner and write the idempotent reattach semantics.

Nina: I'll prototype partition alignment tests and alert-window simulations.

Alex: awesome. I'll post RFC draft by EOD and set a 30-min sync tomorrow. If anyone sees a hard blocker, ping here. :raised_hands:
